final_message:
I fixed one bug in `wrap` in `src/wrap.py`: it emitted a spurious empty line whenever a word was longer than `width`. I haven't run it or any tests.

The wrap check fired even when the current line was empty. A word wider than `width` appended `""` to the output and then started its line. The check now only fires when there's already text on the line: `if cur and len(cur) + extra > width:`.

Words longer than `width` are still kept whole on their own line rather than split. If you want them broken at `width`, tell me and I'll add that.
